non_econ_governance.label: Non-economic factors (1): corruption, weak institutions and political instability

stages.name: Role of NGOs
stages.title: Role of NGOs
stages.sub: Explain why NGOs exist alongside government aid and how they reach people that official aid struggles to reach.

steps.q: A government promises bilateral aid to a country, but the receiving government is riddled with corruption and the money often goes missing before it reaches villages. Does the promised aid reliably reach the people who need it?
steps.right: No, a lot of it fails to arrive
steps.hint: Think about what corruption and weak institutions do to money passed between governments.
steps.pre: So even when aid is promised, there is often a

steps.q: A small charity sends its own staff directly into remote villages to hand out food and medicine, rather than giving money to the national government first. Is this money more or less likely to reach ordinary people than aid routed through officials?
steps.right: More likely, it goes straight to people
steps.wrong: Less likely, officials are more reliable
steps.hint: Who is actually carrying out the work in this example?
steps.pre: Delivering aid directly to communities on the ground is called

steps.q: A charity publishes exactly how many blankets and vaccines it bought with donors' money, and donors can check this themselves. Compare this to money that just vanishes inside a corrupt ministry: which is easier for donors to track and question?
steps.right: The charity's spending is easier to track
steps.wrong: Both are equally easy to track
steps.hint: One has public reporting to donors; the other passes through weak institutions with little oversight.

steps.q: Given that charities can deliver aid straight to communities and report clearly to donors, even in countries with corrupt or unstable governments, what part do they play in development?
steps.right: They fill gaps official aid and weak governments leave
steps.wrong: They simply hand their money to the government to distribute
steps.hint: Think about what local delivery plus accountability lets these organisations do that government-to-government aid cannot.
